# Half-finger single-hand composite fixture

`composite.png` is **generated by `build_fixture.py`**, not a downloaded image. It contains no external
image, no trademarked render and no game asset — the same claim `../glove_sport_v1/LICENSE.md` makes, and
for the same reason: a fixture that needs a licensed file is a fixture that cannot run on a fresh checkout
or in CI.

What it reproduces is the *structure* of a marketplace listing, which is what the code under test has to
cope with:

| property | why it is here |
|---|---|
| two views stacked in one image | the same path submitted twice yields one pHash, sets `duplicateOfHash`, and is refused — so a composite must be split before intake |
| a caption band between them | rejected by shape (wide, short) rather than by position, so it survives a different layout |
| a tiled watermark | rejected by area as a region, and dropped from the crop by connected-component membership. It is also why the splitter masks by distance from the backdrop rather than reusing `build_foreground_mask`, whose saturation clause admits a navy backdrop's watermark and joins every subject into one component |
| a saturated dark backdrop | `check_reference_admission` segments against a sampled corner background; a crop that keeps this backdrop reports `foregroundCoverage 1.000` and is refused as not isolable |
| **one** glove, not a pair | the hand is declared, never inferred: `measure_silhouette` reads only the largest foreground component, so a single glove and a pair look the same to it |
| digits cut off flat | `formProfile.kind: fingerless` with every digit `open-cut`, including the thumb |

Regenerate with:

```bash
python3 forge/tests/fixtures/glove_hydra_v1/build_fixture.py
```

It rewrites `composite.png`, `plates/`, `split-provenance.json` and `observation.json` together, so the
observation's `sourceHash` values cannot drift from the plates they describe.

A run against the real item's listing image is local-only, because that image is Valve art and does not
belong in the repository. Point `--composite` at it:

```bash
python3 forge/tests/run_glove_item.py \
    --composite <listing.png> --roles dorsal palmar --hand left \
    --subtype hydra-gloves --observation <observation.json> \
    --out-dir .img2threejs/hydra-fn-v1
```

## What the split cannot do, and it shows in a render

A watermark tile that **overlaps** the glove is connected to it, so it is part of the subject's own
component and survives into the plate — and from there the surface bake projects it onto the model. The
fixture is deliberately drawn with tiles that do both: some sit clear of the glove and are dropped, some
cross it and are not.

Removing the overlapping ones would mean inventing the pixels underneath. That is a different operation
from choosing a rectangle, and this module does not do it. The consequence is a texture carrying the
listing's watermark where it crossed the item, which is one more reason `SKILL.md` requires form to be
judged on an **untextured** render.
